commit.message:
Show every install variant on the getting started page (#23018)

The same change as #23012 on main, for this branch.

### What is wrong today

The Installation section gives one command, `pip install executorch`,
and that command
does not produce a working setup.

PyTorch is not installed with it. The package does not declare torch as
a dependency,
because the right build depends on the hardware. In a clean environment
the export
example a few paragraphs further down the same page stops with
`No module named 'torch'`.

The CUDA packages are not mentioned anywhere on the page, although this
branch publishes
`cu130`, `cu132` and `cu134`. To find any of them today you have to
already know how the
package index is laid out.

### What this changes

The single command becomes one command template plus a small table of
variants, in the
spirit of the PyTorch get started page. You find the row for the machine
you export on and
put its name in the index URL.

The table is the same as main's, because #23016 made the published list
on this branch
match main. One paragraph differs: the nightly one names no variants,
since nightly builds
are built from `main` and can cover a different set, and it leaves out
main's note that
13.4 is nightly only, which is not true on this branch.

A test is added next to the existing release matrix checks: the CUDA
versions named in that
section must be exactly the ones this branch publishes. The page then
cannot drift from the
build, on this branch or on any branch it is copied to.

### What was tested

`pytest .ci/scripts/tests/test_filter_cuda_matrix.py` passes, 26 cases.
The new case fails
when a row is removed from the table.

Every documented variant was installed with `pip install --dry-run` in a
clean environment,
and the resolved executorch and torch versions come from the intended
index: `cpu`, `cu130`
and `cu132` from the release index, `cu134` from nightly, since the
first stable `cu134`
wheels are the ones this branch will publish.

The old instruction was confirmed broken: `pip install executorch` in a
clean environment
installs no torch, and `import executorch.exir` then fails.

+        page = ROOT / "docs" / "source" / "getting-started.md"

+        heading = "\n## Installation\n"
+        self.assertIn(heading, text, f"no Installation section in {page.name}")

+        self.assertEqual(
+            documented,
+            set(FILTER.SUPPORTED_CUDA_VERSIONS),
+            f"the install table in {page.name} lists {sorted(documented)}",

+Both packages come from the same package index. Find your machine in the table

 ```
-pip install executorch --pre --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cpu
+pip install executorch torch \
+  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/<variant> \
+  --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple
 ```
 
+| Machine you export on | Variant |
+| --- | --- |
+| CPU only | `cpu` |
+| NVIDIA GPU, CUDA 13.0 | `cu130` |
+| NVIDIA GPU, CUDA 13.2 | `cu132` |
+| NVIDIA GPU, CUDA 13.4 | `cu134` |
+
+The CUDA packages are built for Linux, on x86_64 and ARM64. Use the `cpu`
+variant on macOS and on Windows. If your CUDA version is not in the table,
+choose the closest lower one with the same major version, because CUDA works
+across minor versions but not across major ones. There is no package for CUDA
+12, so on CUDA 12 use the `cpu` variant or build from source.
+
+To get a change that has landed on the `main` branch but is not in this release,
+use a nightly build. These are rebuilt every day. Put `nightly/` in front of the
+variant name, for example `nightly/cu130`, and add `--pre` to the command,
+otherwise pip skips development versions. Nightly builds follow `main`, so the
+set of variants they cover can differ from the table above.
+
+The second index is needed because a bare `--index-url` replaces PyPI instead of
+adding to it, and some dependencies are published only on PyPI.
+
 To build the framework from source, see [Building From Source](using-executorch-building-from-source.md). Backend delegates may require additional dependencies. See the appropriate backend documentation for more information.
 
 > **_NOTE:_** On Windows, ExecuTorch requires a [Visual Studio Developer Powershell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/ide/reference/command-prompt-powershell?view=vs-2022). Running from outside of a developer prompt will manifest as errors related to CL.exe.
